## Getting started

Install sqlpipe with a single command:

```sh
curl -sSL https://get.sqlpipe.dev | sh
```

This downloads the latest release and places the `sqlpipe` binary on your `PATH`. Verify the installation with `sqlpipe --version`.

Next, create a `sqlpipe.yaml` file in your project directory. This is where you define your source and target connections and the pipelines between them. A minimal example:

```yaml
source:
  type: postgres
  dsn: postgres://user:pass@localhost:5432/mydb
target:
  type: mysql
  dsn: user:pass@tcp(localhost:3306)/mydb
```

Adjust the connection details to match your databases. Keep credentials out of version control: reference environment variables where possible.

Finally, start your first run:

```sh
sqlpipe run --config sqlpipe.yaml
```

sqlpipe connects to both databases, validates the configuration, and begins transferring data. Progress and any errors are logged to stdout.
